With --identity, as C2 flies, the gate is follow_vlm.Reacquirer with no anchor: 10 identity-ok boxes in a row within 30 m (twice the node's --start-when-seen 5), of one object (each within 3 m + 3 m/s x the time since the last pick) and seen moving, an inference with no acceptable box or a box of another place restarting the streak, a place seen not to move refused; its streak and refusals are metrics.json start_gate.identity_gate. A run flown with --identity whose metrics.json start_gate records no `rule` was flown before the node stated this rule: its [start] line printed the pixel gate's streak and a timeout's end_reason reads '5 inferences in a row', though the rule above is the one that decided

the hand-written estimator follow on the same rail (--pilot servo --target-estimator, FAMILY=estimator; added 2026-11-17, after the C2 flights of 16 November): the lab's own no-learning follow - the perception node's EstimatorFollowPilot, follow_vlm.fly()'s servo on the target estimate with its strict lock and re-acquisition and its trail-following forward direction - kept apart from the box-servo null, with no lost end; not all of fly(), so not equal to the lab's follow
C2_follow_closed_loop.estimator_null_as_flown: The estimator null is the perception node's EstimatorFollowPilot (demo/pas_ardupilot/perception_node.py, --pilot servo --mission follow --identity --target-estimator): demo/subject_track.SubjectTrack's target estimator, strict lock and Reacquirer - the same ones the C2 VLA flights fly - and follow_vlm.fly()'s two track branches on them (the servo on the estimate, with the line-of-sight and range feed-forwards, the catch-up and the stopped-subject floor; else the box servo at the same metric stand-off), then a coast toward the subject's memory (the last track speed decaying, a backing-off aircraft still backing) and the servo pilot's sweep. Its forward speed is flown as fly()'s --trail-follow flies it, on by default as agx_manual_20261103 flew it (trail ticks 3570 of its 4197): toward a carrot trail_lookahead_m (10 m) along the subject's trail (trail.direction), never away from the served estimate, else along the nose; the run records its trail ticks (metrics.json estimator_follow.trail_ticks). The launcher gives it --want-width 0.16 and --speed-max 5, the values of agx_manual_20261103 (follow_vlm.py on simple_flight, 0.952 within 30 m). It is NOT all of fly(), so not equal to the lab's follow: the trail approach in the coast and the search, the search sweep closed on the lookout, the search creep and planner, FenceGuard (its gate and smoothing, and clear_aim, which keeps fly()'s aim out of the zones' bands), the slew limiter and the orbit are not ported (the Shield and ArduPilot stand there), and its line-of-sight rate without a measured velocity uses its own last command where fly() used the guard's emitted one. It has no lost end: it flies to max_s and is replayed under the VLAs' end rule as the box-servo null is
C2_follow_closed_loop.null_as_flown: The null is the perception node's FollowPilot (demo/pas_ardupilot/perception_node.py, --pilot servo --mission follow --identity, no --target-estimator: with one the run is the estimator null): a box-width P-servo (follow_vlm.servo) at the node's defaults, want_width 0.10 and speed_max 4.0 m/s, which deploy/orin/run_pas_perception.sh does not override. It has no target estimator, no target lock (with --identity and no estimator the Grounder runs no lock), and no lost end: with no fresh box it searches - forward 0, a yaw sweep - and flies on to max_s. It is NOT the follow_vlm estimator follow (want_width 0.16, speed_max 5.0, a target estimator, catch-up and a search planner, e.g. agx_manual_20261103 on simple_flight) behind the older hand-written numbers of 0.95-0.98 within 30 m: that follow's stand-in on this rail is the estimator null
C2_follow_closed_loop.null_under_the_vla_end_rule: the null has no lost end, so beside its share as flown each null flight is replayed under the VLAs' own end rule from its own files: a tick's wall time is its flight_log.jsonl `t` plus the one offset that puts every tick at or after the detections.jsonl row its `det_seq` names (the largest row t - tick t); a tick has a fresh box when the newest detections.jsonl row with a box published by then was captured (t_capture, else t_cap) at most det_fresh_s before it; the flight ends on the first tick lost_timeout_s after the last tick with a fresh box (after the first tick if none had one); and the share within 30 m is the node's, over the ticks up to that one whose subject pose was read. lost_timeout_s and det_fresh_s are the ones every C2 VLA flight records (metrics.json vla.mission.monitor.config); the column is shown only when they all record them and the same replay ends each C2 VLA flight within 5 s of where its own monitor did
C2_follow_closed_loop.gate_timeouts: a flight that would be C2 but for a start gate that timed out (its only other faults the ones a flight with no mission gets: its rail's topology stamp, and kpi.json grade reasons that say no mission was flown) is censored: listed, counted beside its backend's C2 flights, not scored and not counted toward its 3; the protocol flies another in its place. A flight of the null is never censored, and one of a backend that is not a row is never listed as censored: neither has a C2 count to stand beside (a timed-out flight of either is in the list of flights that are not C2)
C2_follow_closed_loop.not_separated: the detector supplies the hint, and while it has no box the model is not asked: a C2 score is the model's and the detector's together

aerialvla_serving.choice: demo/vla_server_v2.py refuses to load the model until --precision, --attn and --merge/--no-merge are all given, and every response's identity carries the chosen configuration's agreement with the reference. Which configuration flies is decided by measuring CityLife's own VRAM beside the model (next wave): the bf16 rows fit only if the renderer and OWL-ViT leave about 17 GB of the 24 GB card free.
aerialvla_serving.choice_note: Why there is no default, and what each option costs (decided 2026-10-22, review of V1a). The precision changes what the model says: bf16 reproduces the upstream-precision reference - bf16/sdpa/unmerged gives the reference's output on 96 % of the 48 probe inputs, the merged bf16 rows on 88-90 % (greedy near-ties) - while every nf4 row agrees on only 25-33 % exactly and 48-50 % within 3 bins; 4-bit quantisation, not the attention kernel or the merge, is what moves the outputs. On the no-hint phrase every bf16 row and both nf4 merged rows answer '00 49 49 LAND' on 5 of 6 frames, while the nf4 unmerged loader (the one every earlier AerialVLA script here used) reproduces two of the 4 Aug malformed landing outputs ('00 49 4949', '00 49 494 49'); the strict reader turns those into holds. nf4/sdpa/merged is kept as the measured low-VRAM option (p50 517 ms; about 7.9 GB held by the process, 5.4 GB of it allocated by torch), not as a default that silently changes behaviour. A bf16 process holds about 16.8-16.9 GB: bf16/sdpa/unmerged (p50 486 ms) is the closest to the reference, bf16/sdpa/merged the fastest (p50 259 ms, below the paper's 0.35 s; its nvidia-smi reading failed, so its process VRAM is not recorded). The 10 GB budget behind the low-VRAM rule is an assumption, not a measurement: the card has 24 GB, desktop applications held about 3.4 GB before the runs (one reading, subtracted from every row's nvidia-smi figure), OWL-ViT takes 0.61 GB, and CityLife's own VRAM has never been logged. Measuring CityLife's VRAM beside the model is what decides which configuration flies (next wave); until then the server loads none by default.
